inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 157.054m shares issued and outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q1 FY2027 10-Q balance sheet) plus 1.128m dilutive securities (Q1 FY2027 diluted less basic weighted average, 157.928m - 156.800m). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The treasury-method increment was measured at the Q1 average price, so it is slightly low at a price near the $73 deal consideration.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K non-GAAP reconciliation, 'Stock based compensation, inclusive of employer taxes' $42.637m (TECH_Annual_FY2026.txt:2733); cash-flow add-back is $41.104m (line 2678). The company's own combined figure is used; the $12.1m of taxes paid on RSU net-share settlement (financing) is NOT added on top, per the no-double-sum rule.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-year US Treasury) + beta ~1.1 x ~4.5% ERP gives a cost of equity near 9.3%; debt is a $200m revolver draw against $350m cash, so the capital structure is effectively all-equity and WACC is set at 9.0%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios - risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: the ~$22.8m annual lease expense is already inside operating expenses and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path. Lease liabilities ($85.6m) are NOT in net debt and no separate lease line is deducted - one treatment, charged once.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: Interest income ($4.2m FY2026) is not deducted from last_fcf because net cash ($150m) is below 1x the FCF base. It does not matter for the forward build: the component flows are unlevered operating flows and contain no interest income.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (Drivers route), three standalone scenarios. Bio-Techne is an operating life-science reagents / instruments / diagnostics company, so the owner-FCF engine is the right engine for the business. DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE ROUTING TABLE: a live takeover normally routes to a deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting. Per the build instruction (and the RWC.AX precedent) the three scenarios here are STANDALONE going-concern values - i.e. what the shares are worth if the Merck KGaA merger does not close - and the deal framing is carried separately in the `deal_analysis` block and `valuation_philosophy`. `weighted_iv`, `upside` and the entry price are therefore NOT a forecast of what a holder receives: if the merger closes the holder receives $73.00 cash regardless of this model. ANCHORS: price from Yahoo chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close, not an after-hours print); cash $350.0m and debt $200.0m (revolver, reclassified to short-term - matures 2027-08-31) from the 2026-09-30 balance sheet in the Q1 FY2027 10-Q; FY0 revenue and flows from the FY2026 10-K. EBITDA BASIS: adjusted operating income FY2026 = segment operating income $397.1m - corporate $11.0m = $386.1m (31.8% of sales), plus depreciation ~$36.2m = adjusted EBITDA ~$422m (34.7%), before SBC and before amortization of acquired intangibles ($61.2m). The margin path starts ~1pp BELOW that because restructuring ($12m / $28m / $21m in FY2024-26), litigation and acquisition costs recur every year at this company and are real cash. D&A path is TOTAL D&A (8.0% of sales in FY2026) declining as acquired-intangible amortization rolls off; that calibrates the cash tax: EBIT after full D&A and SBC of ~$282m x 23% = ~$65m vs $64.1m income taxes actually paid in FY2026. WORKING CAPITAL: receivables + inventory exceed payables (NWC ~22% of sales), so growth consumes cash: wc_capture is negative. BUYBACKS: $41.7m in FY2026 ($275.7m in FY2025); repurchases are contractually restricted while the Merger Agreement is in effect, so the flat count is currently a modelling convention rather than a funded one. WILSON WOLF: the 19.9% equity-method stake is added in the bridge at book ($230.6m) because its earnings are not in the operating flows. The contractual purchase of the remaining 80.1% by 2027-12-31 (~$1bn at ~4.4x trailing revenue, plus possible contingent consideration) is treated as value-neutral - cash out equals asset in at the contract price - and is neither deducted nor credited. That is the largest unmodelled item: it would turn net cash of $150m into net debt of roughly $0.85bn and add a high-margin cell-therapy consumables business; whether 4.4x revenue is accretive depends on Wilson Wolf financials that are not disclosed in the filings.

equity_bridge.item: Wilson Wolf 19.9% equity-method investment at book
equity_bridge.note: Q1 FY2027 10-Q fair-value/other-assets note (TECH_Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt:1430), 2026-09-30. Its income is excluded from the operating flows, so the asset is added here (matching-asset rule). Acquired for $232m + $25m forward premium in FY2022-23; contract price for the remaining 80.1% implies a similar or higher value.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3-year equity CAGR (+2.3%) diverges from 3-year GAAP EPS CAGR (-13.0%): FY2023 EPS ($1.76) was inflated by investment gains while FY2024-26 GAAP EPS carried impairments of held-for-sale assets, a $37m arbitration award and restructuring. On the 5-year window equity (6.1%), revenue (5.5%) and EPS (5.9%) agree, which is why the 5-year equity rate is selected.
historical_growth.notes: FY2026 vs FY2023 and FY2021 (June year-ends; per-share figures on the post-November-2022 4:1 split basis). FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2021 $256.0m, FY2023 $174.9m, FY2026 $220.6m. Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are close because SBC has been flat at ~$40-52m for six years - SBC is not growing faster than cash flow. FY2021 was a COVID-era peak (17% organic growth in FY2022 followed), so the negative 5-year FCF CAGR is a peak-to-trough artefact; owner FCF has been in a $175-256m band while revenue grew 30%, reflecting margin compression from ~38% to ~32% adjusted operating margin.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 = FY2027: Q1 reported +5% (+7% organic, Protein Sciences +9%); no formal guidance, so the year is held at the Q1 reported rate rather than extrapolating one strong quarter against an easy comparison (Q1 FY2026 organic -1%). Then mid-single-digit growth in line with the 5-year revenue and equity CAGRs (5.5-6.1%), fading to 3.5%.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC) was ~34.7% in FY2026; path starts 1.2pp lower to carry recurring restructuring/litigation cash, and recovers to 36% - still well short of the ~41% of FY2022 - as volume returns to a 75%-gross-margin reagent franchise.
base.capex_rationale: FY2027: $5.9m in Q1 + ~$28m guided for the remaining three quarters = ~$34m (2.7%). 3.0% thereafter vs 2.4-5.4% over FY2024-26.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax FY2026 $64.1m = ~23% of owner EBIT; guidance 23-27% ETR before discrete items. No abnormal shelter to unwind; the falling D&A path removes the amortization shield on its own.

scenario_narratives.base: STANDALONE (merger does not close). The Q1 FY2027 re-acceleration (+7% organic, Protein Sciences +9%) proves to be demand stabilising after a flat FY2026 rather than a new trend: core research reagents (R&D Systems, Novus, Tocris) grow mid-single digits as biotech funding and academic budgets normalise, ProteinSimple instruments and cGMP proteins for cell therapy add a point or two, and Diagnostics and Spatial Biology stays a low-single-digit, sub-scale segment with a ~55% gross margin. Adjusted EBITDA margin recovers from ~34% to 36% on volume leverage but never regains the ~41% of FY2022, because pricing and mix pressure in Protein Sciences (organic -1% in FY2026) are structural consequences of being sub-scale against Thermo Fisher and Danaher. Recurring restructuring and litigation costs are treated as real. Wilson Wolf is bought at the contract price and earns its cost of capital.
scenario_narratives.bull: STANDALONE. Bio-Techne returns to the high-single-digit organic growth it delivered before FY2023: spatial biology (RNAscope plus Lunaphore COMET) scales into a profitable franchise instead of a margin drag, cGMP proteins and the Wilson Wolf G-Rex / ScaleReady channel ride commercial cell-therapy approvals, NIH funding is resolved without cuts and China stabilises. Operating leverage on a 75%-gross-margin consumables base takes adjusted EBITDA margin back to 40%. This is roughly the business Merck KGaA is underwriting - before its own ~EUR 140m of cost synergies, which a standalone shareholder never receives - and it needs several independent things to go right.
scenario_narratives.bear: STANDALONE. The deal breaks into a weak tape: NIH indirect-cost caps and flat academic budgets hold US research demand down (US revenue already fell 7% in FY2026), China remains a ~$100m market that does not grow, pharma/biotech customers consolidate reagent vendors toward Thermo Fisher, Danaher/Abcam and MilliporeSigma, and Protein Sciences pricing keeps eroding. Diagnostics and Spatial Biology continues to need restructuring and divestitures (Exosome Diagnostics, held-for-sale impairments). Growth runs at 2-3.5% and adjusted EBITDA margin settles at 32%, with a lower terminal multiple for a sub-scale, ex-growth tools company. Not a solvency case - the balance sheet is net cash before the Wilson Wolf purchase - so the terminal value does not approach the zero floor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: These weight the STANDALONE outcomes only; deal-completes vs deal-breaks is handled in deal_analysis, not here. Bear 20% (above the 15% house default): FY2026 organic growth was flat with Protein Sciences down 1%, and the largest customer group depends on a single funder (NIH) whose policy is in litigation. Base 50%: one quarter of +7% organic growth against an easy comparison supports stabilisation, not more. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs spatial biology profitability, cell-therapy adoption and research funding all to go right at once.

entry_price.method: Standalone hurdle entry price: terminal value rebuilt at the 15% hurdle. Not actionable while the merger is pending - the stock trades on the $73.00 cash consideration, and a 15% return from a standalone holding is only reachable after a deal break and a fall well below the pre-announcement price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Bio-Techne is the subject of a signed, shareholder-approved, all-cash merger with Merck KGaA at $73.00 per share (announced 2026-06-25; US HSR waiting period expired 2026-09-18; Bundeskartellamt cleared; shareholder vote 2026-09-23; close expected late 2026 / early 2027). The share price therefore measures the probability and timing of receiving $73.00, not the value of the business. This model answers a different question: what the shares are worth on their own cash flows if the merger fails. On the house basis (SBC expensed, 9% WACC, terminal multiple capped at 20x) the standalone value is far below the deal price in every scenario, including the bull case. The 'upside' figure the dashboard derives from weighted IV versus price is therefore the size of the downside to model value on a deal break, NOT a signal that the stock is overvalued in the ordinary sense: a holder who keeps the shares to completion receives $73.00 whatever this model says. The gap is the control premium - Merck is paying roughly 27x FY2026 adjusted EBITDA and about 36% over the one-month pre-announcement VWAP for strategic fit, scale and ~EUR 140m of cost synergies that only an acquirer can extract. The house standalone value is also below the pre-announcement market price (the ~$54 implied by that premium), which is normal for this model on premium-multiple life-science tools names: the market capitalised Bio-Techne at 30x+ owner FCF before the bid, and the model caps the exit at 20x. Practical reading: (1) at a price pinned just under $73.00 the remaining return to completion is a small, time-value-sized spread; (2) the loss on a break is large - toward the pre-deal trading range in the first instance, and toward this model's values if the market also re-rates the sector; (3) for a long-term owner there is no margin of safety here and no reason to own the shares other than merger arbitrage, and for an existing holder selling near $73.00 versus waiting is a trade of a few weeks' interest against a low-probability, high-severity break.
key_risks_to_valuation: Deal completion is the only variable that matters for a holder: remaining regulatory approvals (China SAMR and other jurisdictions are not confirmed in the filings) and the Outside Date. On a regulatory failure Merck owes a ~$576.1m reverse termination fee (~$3.6 per share pre-tax), which cushions but does not offset a break.

Standalone value is sensitive to the terminal assumption: the base case is ~60% terminal value at a 17x Gordon multiple; the pre-deal market paid materially more for the franchise than this model does.

Wilson Wolf: the ~$1bn purchase of the remaining 80.1% by 2027-12-31 is treated as value-neutral at the contract price. If 4.4x trailing revenue proves cheap for a high-margin cell-therapy consumables business the standalone value is understated; if cell-therapy demand disappoints it is overstated, and the purchase would take the company from net cash to roughly $0.85bn of net debt.
Margin path: adjusted operating margin has fallen from ~38% (FY2022) to ~32% (FY2026). The base case assumes only a partial recovery; each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly $1 per share.

Recurring 'non-recurring' charges: restructuring, litigation and acquisition costs have run $25-83m a year; the base margin path carries ~1.2pp of revenue for them, which may be too little or too much on a standalone basis.
Research-funding dependence (NIH indirect-cost litigation), China (~9% of sales) and ~48% of revenue in foreign currencies.

deal_analysis.approvals_outstanding: Other required antitrust / foreign-investment clearances; China SAMR status not confirmed in public filings
deal_analysis.capital_return_restrictions: Buybacks and dividend changes require Merck KGaA consent while the Merger Agreement is in effect
deal_analysis.how_to_read_the_dcf: valuation.*, probability_weighted.weighted_iv and entry_price are STANDALONE (deal-breaks) values. Deal-completes value is the $73.00 consideration. A deal-weighted value is p x 73.00 + (1 - p) x break value; see deal_weighted_value.

deal_weighted_value.formula: p x 73.00 + (1 - p) x break value, undiscounted
deal_weighted_value.note: Excludes the reverse termination fee and time value. A market price within a few tenths of a dollar of the consideration implies the market is pricing completion at roughly 98-99%; the asymmetry is a spread measured in cents against a break loss of roughly $19 (to the pre-announcement level) to $35 (to model standalone value) per share.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular-session close); 52-week range 43.20-72.88, the high being the deal-pinned level
data_sources.financials: TECH_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL); FY2026 10-K (TECH_Annual_FY2026.txt) for the non-GAAP reconciliation, segment note, SBC, cash taxes and merger terms; Q1 FY2027 10-Q filed 2026-11-06 (TECH_Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt) for the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, share count, Wilson Wolf carrying value and capex / tax-rate outlook
